issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting information about the type of the Animal.name attribute: the UML diagram specifies the attribute as type String, whereas the textual instructions explicitly require using StringBuilder. The provided reference solution (Animal.java) implements the attribute as a String. This mismatch (UML vs. textual requirement vs. solution) can confuse students about which type to use and how to implement getters/setters and subclass code that accesses the name.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose and document a single type for the Animal.name attribute. Either: (A) Keep String (update the textual instruction to remove the StringBuilder requirement and ensure the UML shows name: String), or (B) Adopt StringBuilder consistently (update the UML to name: StringBuilder, adjust the reference solution Animal.java to use a private StringBuilder name and provide appropriate getter/setter and subclasses that use getName()/toString()). Apply the chosen change across the problem statement, template, and solution to keep all artifacts consistent.
